chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: Hello! So you want to learn how to make websites. In that case, you need to learn HTML.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: Let's start at the very beginning. What exactly is HTML? And why do I need it? Let's break it

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: down from the basics and build our way up. HTML stands for Hypertext Markup Language. It uses markup

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: to describe the structure of web pages. The structure is built up by elements and they are

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: represented by tags, tags label pieces of content such as heading, paragraph, table and so on.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: These tags aren't shown in the page but are used to display content in different ways.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: That's a lot to digest, so let's go into it. First, let's try it together. Don't worry about

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: understanding. It'll all click as we work through it. We start by declaring that this is an HTML

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: document. The HTML is the root element of any HTML page. The head contained meta information about

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: the document. The title element specifies a title for the document. The body contains the visible

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: page content. Finally, the H1 defines a large heading while P defines a paragraph. With everything

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: set in the order, let's go into the explanation of how tags work. Tags typically come in pairs,

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: a start tag and the end tag. The end tag is written just like the start tag but with a forward

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: slash inserted before the tag name. Here we've got the tag name and the forward slash tag name

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: and the content of the element in between them. So this was a paragraph we'd use P, forward slash

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: P and some text in the middle. Let's play a game. See if we can correctly match, start and end tags

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: together. So what turns HTML code and elements into a viewable website? Well, that's where web

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: browsers come in. The purpose of a web browser, be it Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari, is to read

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: HTML documents and display them. But the browser does not display the HTML code. Instead, it uses it

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: to determine how to display the document. Let's see what kind of building blocks are hidden behind

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: this web page. This is a visualization of an HTML page structure. You can see the HTML,

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: the head, with the page title below that, and then the body under that.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: And that's the basics. Let's delve into this further. But for now, take a break.
